## TL;DR

This resumed pass closes the review gap for #1210: it declares the normal,
warning, and critical pressure fixtures at both 1280×900 and 375×900. The first
handoff had only an automatic capture of the un-fixtured dashboard, which showed
the resource panel waiting for data. The review found no code defect and
confirmed the state copy, metric formatting, and CLI explanations were already
covered. The failure was evidence coverage, so I updated the task's declared
shots without changing application code.

## Work and rationale

I read the latest review report and the existing pressure QA note before making
changes. The review called for six distinct fixture and viewport combinations,
and specifically noted that mobile captures must show the panel after it is
brought into view. The `repoos update 1210 --shots` command accepted six entries:
the three `system:pressure*` states at 1280×900 and the same states at 375×900.
Each entry names the default app target, `/` route, `.resource-panel` selector,
and the same highlight selector, giving the capture process a specific element
to render and frame.

I retained the existing source implementation and regression tests because the
review's evidence says there were no code defects. The current QA note already
describes what the states mean: normal is clear, warning is advisory and does
not hold work, and critical pressure holds new starts while leaving running
agents alone. It also records that swap, compressor, and available-memory
readings appear in every state, while the critical state carries the active and
queued heavy-job details. Changing any of those behaviors during an evidence
repair would have expanded scope without a review finding to address.

The earlier session's documentation reports a headless Chromium pass against
the auth-less server with synthetic fixtures at both viewport widths. The review
did not accept that as handoff evidence because those visits were not declared
shots. This resumed turn therefore treats the declaration itself as the
necessary correction; it does not claim to have re-run or independently observed
those browser visits here. No visible browser was opened, and this turn did not
start a server or alter the fixtures.

## Approaches tried

I first checked the task's live RepoOS status and handoff result, then inspected
the worktree's task copy, its latest review report, and the pressure QA document.
The current board lists #1210 as active after the review returned it for fixes.
The handoff status explains that the prior request failed because the required
engineering report draft was missing. The review artifact supplies the remaining
actionable issue: declared state captures at the two target widths.

I used RepoOS's metadata command to update the shot declaration rather than
editing task frontmatter or the `## Shots` section directly. This preserves the
repo's task metadata workflow and provides machine-readable capture definitions.
I kept all six combinations explicit because review needs to distinguish each
state at each viewport. The panel is the selected and highlighted element for
every entry, so mobile framing centers on the target instead of relying on a
top-of-page screenshot that might leave it below the fold.

## Challenges and blockers

The task file inside the assigned worktree still shows its earlier status and
does not reflect the latest central board metadata. RepoOS warned that its CLI
was reading the main checkout's board while processing `repoos update`; I did
not manually inspect or edit the main checkout. The command reported the shot
update as accepted, and I left the worktree's tracked task copy alone because
RepoOS owns metadata synchronization and the workflow explicitly forbids manual
task-file edits.

The prior handoff also reported a missing engineering report draft. This file
addresses that specific blocker in the required format. I have not treated the
earlier session's reported browser checks as fresh verification in this turn.
The required scoped `repoos check` remains the final gate for the source tree.

## Key learnings

Fixture-based manual browser visits and task handoff captures serve different
purposes. A successful manual pass can establish that states render, but it does
not give the reviewer a stable set of screenshots unless the states and
viewports are declared through RepoOS. For this QA task, the panel must also be
the explicit capture target at mobile width so reviewers can inspect it in the
viewport. When review identifies an evidence gap and no source defect, keep the
repair narrow: declare the missing evidence, retain the verified implementation
and tests, and state exactly which results were observed in the current turn.
